chapters.chapter_title: Describe Image: Planning, Fluency, Pronunciation, and Timed Practice

estimated_study_time.text: Plan for about 2 hours of focused study, plus extra time for recording and reviewing your own 40-second responses.

chapter_summary.text: This lesson provides skills practice for the PTE Academic Describe image item type. It focuses on speaking for a purpose, organizing oral presentations logically, developing complex spoken ideas, using appropriate words and correct grammar, speaking naturally, and using correct intonation, pronunciation, and stress. It also includes listening practice in following an oral sequence of information.

evidence_spans.quote: This lesson provides skills practice for the PTE Academic item type Describe image.

Speaking
• Speaking for a purpose (to repeat, to inform, to explain)
• Supporting an opinion with details, examples and explanations
• Organizing an oral presentation in a logical way
• Developing complex ideas within a spoken discourse

Using words and phrases appropriate to the context
• Using correct grammar
• Speaking at a natural rate
• Using correct intonation
• Using correct pronunciation
• Using correct stress

Listening
• Following an oral sequencing of information

meaning.text: Describe image assesses the ability to orally describe an image from an academic source, such as a graph, picture, map, chart, or table.

evidence_spans.quote:
Describe image item type which assesses their ability to 
orally describe an image from an academic source (such as a graph, picture, map, chart or table).

meaning.text: Content is scored according to the ability to accurately and thoroughly describe all aspects and elements of the image.

evidence_spans.quote:
The score for content is based on your ability to accurately 
and thoroughly describe the image. In other words, 
you need to describe all aspects and elements of the 
image.

meaning.text: Oral fluency is the ability to speak smoothly, effortlessly, and naturally, with smooth and accurate rhythm, phrasing, and stress, and without too many pauses, repetitions, false starts, or hesitations.

evidence_spans.quote:
The score for oral fluency is based on your ability to 
speak smoothly, effortlessly and naturally. You need to 
make sure that your rhythm, phrasing and stress are 
smooth and accurate

you can keep speaking 
without too many pauses, repetitions, false starts or 
hesitations.

meaning.text: Pronunciation is the ability to accurately produce sounds and words, including vowels and consonants, word stress, sentence stress, and intonation.

evidence_spans.quote:
The score for pronunciation is based on your ability to 
accurately produce sounds and words. You need to be 
able to correctly pronounce vowels and consonants, 
and to have correct word stress, sentence stress and 
intonation.

explanation.text: For Describe image, test takers have 25 seconds to prepare their description and 40 seconds to give their description.

evidence_spans.quote:
for this item type, they have 25 seconds to prepare for their description and 40 seconds 
to give their description.

core_lessons.title: Plan a graph response before speaking

explanation.text: A graph response can be planned by identifying the speaking purpose, general topic, axis information, unit of measurement, significant information, and remarkable facts in the image.

evidence_spans.quote:
What is your speaking purpose for this task?  (To describe a graph and recount its statistical 
information.)

What is the general topic conveyed by this image? (The populations of Spanish speaking people in 
various countries)

What information is given on the x and y axes? (x axis = the countries, y axis = populations)
– What unit of measurement is used? (millions)

What significant information is conveyed by the image? (Most Spanish speaking countries are in 
Latin America, and Mexico has the greatest number of speakers.)
Are there any remarkable facts given in the graph’s information?

explanation.text: Graph descriptions usually begin with the main topic, then present facts from the x or y axis supported by statistics. If there is a trend or exception, comment on it and support it with data; if there is no obvious trend, describe the graph from left to right, and for pie charts start with the largest piece.

evidence_spans.quote:
Descriptions of graphical 
images usually begin with a sentence that states the main topic, often paraphrased from the title, 
followed by facts from the x or y axis supported by statistics.

If test takers can see a trend or an 
exception, they should comment on it and support what they say with some data.

If test takers 
are describing data that does not have an obvious trend, they should describe a graph from left to 
right, and start with the largest piece of the pie for pie charts.

core_lessons.title: Choose tense from the time information in the image

explanation.text: Use the simple present tense when a graph has no fixed time periods. If fixed time periods are used, such as a comparison of statistics over different specific times, use the simple past tense.

evidence_spans.quote:
The simple present tense 
because the graph has no fixed time periods.

If fixed time periods were used, for example in a 
comparison of statistics over different specific times, the simple past tense would be used.

explanation.text: A photograph description cannot be planned or presented exactly like a graph or pie chart, but some of the same planning questions can still be used. Images that emphasize contrast usually begin with the main topic of contrast and then give examples of differences.

evidence_spans.quote:
since this image is a photo, rather than a graph or pie chart, its 
description cannot be planned or presented in quite the same way as the previous examples.

However, 
some of the same planning questions asked earlier can still be used.

Descriptions of images that 
emphasize contrast usually begin with a sentence that states the main topic of contrast, and then 
give examples of differences.

core_lessons.title: Use stress and intonation to support meaning

explanation.text: In English, meaning is expressed by stressing certain words, generally key words or new information. Word stress matters because stressing an incorrect syllable can create confusion. Intonation also gives meaning and tells the listener the speaker’s intention.

evidence_spans.quote:
in English a lot of meaning is expressed by stressing certain words (i.e. saying them with 
more emphasis and loudly). These are generally key words or new information.

word stress is important as stressing an incorrect syllable in a word can create 
confusion

intonation (i.e. whether the speaker’s voice rises or falls) gives a lot of meaning 
and also tells the listener the speaker’s intention.

explanation.text: During timed practice, one partner speaks while the other listens, assesses the performance with a brief checklist, and gives feedback based on notes made on the checklist.

evidence_spans.quote:
As one 
partner speaks, the other must listen and assess his/her performance by completing a brief checklist.

the 
listening partner listens and assesses, then gives his/her partner feedback based on notes made on 
the checklist.

example.text: Prompt yourself in this order: What is the image type? What is the main topic? What data categories are shown? What numbers or units are important? What is the biggest value? Is there an exception or trend? Then turn those notes into a 40-second description.

explanation.text: The lesson models planning through questions about speaking purpose, topic, axes, units, significant information, and remarkable facts, and states that addressing these questions in order can generate enough language for 40 seconds.

evidence_spans.quote:
What is your speaking purpose for this task?  (To describe a graph and recount its statistical 
information.)
What is the general topic conveyed by this image?

What information is given on the x and y axes? (x axis = the countries, y axis = populations)
– What unit of measurement is used? (millions)
What significant information is conveyed by the image?

by addressing each of these questions in order, they can successfully generate 
enough language for the 40 seconds required.

example.text: Start with the contrast: “The image contrasts an older building with a newer building.” Then describe visible differences such as height, materials, style, surface, and position.

explanation.text: For photographs that emphasize contrast, the lesson recommends beginning with the main topic of contrast and then giving examples of differences; it also gives possible contrasting adjectives such as old/new, high/low, smooth/rough, and modern/classical.

evidence_spans.quote:
Descriptions of images that 
emphasize contrast usually begin with a sentence that states the main topic of contrast, and then 
give examples of differences.

What are some contrasting adjectives that might be used to refer to both buildings? (‘old/new’, 
‘high/low’, ‘smooth/rough’, ‘modern/classical’)

worked_examples.title: Using a model response to notice organization

example.text: After recording your answer, compare it with a sample response. Check whether both answers begin with the main topic, select relevant details, use figures accurately, and use appropriate grammar and vocabulary.

explanation.text: The lesson asks test takers to compare their descriptions with models and reflect on introductions, information, organization, vocabulary, and grammar.

evidence_spans.quote:
Ask test takers to 
compare their descriptions with the models and to reflect on whether they used similar introductions, 
information, organization, vocabulary and grammar.

misconception.text: Describe image is scored only on content, so pronunciation and fluency do not matter.

correction.text: Describe image is scored according to three factors: content, oral fluency, and pronunciation.

evidence_spans.quote:
The Describe image item type is scored according to 
three factors:
• Content
• Oral fluency
• Pronunciation

misconception.text: A good graph response can list numbers in any order without an opening topic sentence.

correction.text: Descriptions usually begin with a sentence stating the main topic and then give image details supported by figures.

evidence_spans.quote:
descriptions usually begin with a sentence 
that states the main topic (often from the title), then give details about the image which are supported 
by figures.

misconception.text: Word stress and sentence stress are optional because the listener can still understand the words.

correction.text: Pronunciation includes producing sounds and words accurately, pronouncing vowels and consonants correctly, and using correct word stress, sentence stress, and intonation.

evidence_spans.quote:
The score for pronunciation is based on your ability to 
accurately produce sounds and words. You need to be 
able to correctly pronounce vowels and consonants, 
and to have correct word stress, sentence stress and 
intonation.

question.text: You have 25 seconds to prepare. Look at a graph or chart and write six planning notes: image type, main topic, important labels, unit of measurement, highest or lowest value, and one trend or exception. Then give a 40-second spoken description.

answer.text: A strong answer begins with the main topic, includes relevant figures or labels, comments on a trend or exception if visible, uses an appropriate tense, and continues fluently for close to 40 seconds.

question.text: Record yourself describing a photograph that shows contrast. Start with the main contrast, then give at least three examples of differences you can see.

answer.text: A strong answer states the contrast clearly, then describes visible differences using relevant vocabulary such as old/new, high/low, smooth/rough, or modern/classical where appropriate.

question.text: Listen to a partner’s 40-second response and complete a checklist: main topic sentence, relevant content, logical organization, grammar, range of vocabulary, correct tense, fluency, word and sentence stress, and intonation.

answer.text: Useful feedback names one strength and one specific improvement, such as adding a clearer main-topic sentence, using more precise figures, reducing pauses, or improving sentence stress on key words.

question.text: Read a short Describe image response aloud twice: once stressing nouns and adjectives that carry key information, and once stressing small words such as articles and prepositions. Notice which version is clearer.

answer.text: The clearer version should stress key words and new information rather than small grammatical words.

review_checklist.text: I can explain that Describe image requires 25 seconds of preparation and 40 seconds of speaking.
I can begin a graph description with the main topic and then support details with figures.
I can choose simple present or simple past tense based on whether the image has fixed time periods.
I can describe a photograph by identifying the main topic or contrast and giving specific examples.
I can monitor whether I keep speaking without too many pauses, repetitions, false starts, or hesitations.
I can use word stress, sentence stress, and intonation to make my spoken response clearer.
